identity.title: Three Languages, Three Jobs
identity.description: Understand the primary responsibilities of HTML, CSS, and JavaScript and predict which language should change when a requirement changes.

primaryCapability.statement: Classify structure, presentation, and behavior changes into HTML, CSS, and JavaScript responsibilities.

knows: There are multiple languages used to build web pages
likelyMisconceptions: The three languages are interchangeable or do the same job.

canDo: Correctly classify structure, presentation, and behavior changes
Explain why the three languages are complementary

experience.startingState: The learner sees frontend languages as an undifferentiated mix.
experience.narrativeContext: Learning to see the separate layers of a web interface.
experience.primaryInteraction: Matching requirements to the correct language.
experience.expectedOutcome: The learner can identify which language to use for a given change.

content.text:
Frontend work becomes easier to reason about when you separate responsibilities.

**HTML → structure and meaning**
**CSS → presentation and layout**
**JavaScript → behavior and changing state**

They work together. They are not interchangeable jobs.
content.keyTakeaway: Responsibility separation is the key to managing frontend complexity.

activities.title: Interactive HTML, CSS & JS Layer Stack
activities.instruction: Toggle Structure (HTML), Presentation (CSS), and Behavior (JS) layers to inspect their distinct responsibilities.

content.title: Interactive HTML, CSS & JS Layer Stack
content.description: Toggle Structure (HTML), Presentation (CSS), and Behavior (JS) layers to inspect their distinct responsibilities.

interactive.caption: Toggle Structure (HTML), Presentation (CSS), and Behavior (JS) layers to inspect their distinct responsibilities.

content.question: You want the page to contain the text “Sign in” as a button label. Which language is the most direct place to put that static structure and content?

feedback.correct: Correct. Static page structure and content belong in HTML.
feedback.incorrect: Think about structure and content. Which language is designed for that?

content.question: You want the button to have rounded corners and more space inside it. Which tool is the most direct?

feedback.correct: Correct. Rounded corners and spacing are presentation concerns, so CSS is the direct tool.
feedback.incorrect: Think about presentation and styling. Which language handles how things look?

content.question: You want clicking the button to change the text from “Save” to “Saved”.

options.text: The browser cannot change the page after the first display

feedback.correct: Correct. This requirement is behavior: something should happen because the user interacted with the page.
feedback.incorrect: Think about behavior and interaction. Which language makes things happen?

content.keyTakeaway: You do not need to memorize method names yet. The important idea is that JavaScript can listen for an interaction and change the page.

content.question: The HTML remains, but the CSS is removed. What is the best prediction?

options.text: The page structure can remain, but the custom visual styling disappears.
The button text and heading disappear from the screen completely.
The browser refuses to render the page until a stylesheet is linked.
The click listener in JavaScript is deleted along with the stylesheet.

feedback.correct: Correct. CSS controls presentation. Removing it does not erase the HTML structure.
feedback.incorrect: If you remove the styling language, what happens to the structural language?

content.question: Now remove the JavaScript, but keep the HTML and CSS. What should you expect?

options.text: The button and styles can remain, but the click behavior described by the script no longer happens.
The button and status text disappear because the script is no longer creating them.
CSS automatically takes over and updates the text to 'Saved' when clicked.
The browser displays an error screen instead of rendering the HTML and CSS.

feedback.correct: Correct. The three languages cooperate, but each has a primary responsibility.
feedback.incorrect: If you remove the behavior language, does the structure or presentation break?

content.question:
Match each requirement to the most direct tool:
1. “This heading should be an <h1>.”
2. “This card should use a two-column layout.”
3. “Clicking this button should hide the panel.”

feedback.correct: Correct. Structure → HTML. Presentation/layout → CSS. Behavior → JavaScript.
feedback.incorrect: Review the primary jobs: <h1> is structure, layout is presentation, and hiding on click is behavior.

takeaways: Mental model: HTML describes what the interface is. CSS describes how it is presented. JavaScript describes what it does and how it can change.
Senior habit: When a requirement changes, first ask: Which responsibility changed?
